summary: This restacks a measured but never-landed row win (pooler K-halves bmm: judged 23.2->21.43 at m=128 and 29.94->26.75 at m=256 in ce808e5a) onto master 36c26199, adds an fp32-partials candidate and uses the hardened gate. One check reads cleanly from the two pooler rows' paired ratios plus the printed selector and kernel names, so no companion is needed. The main risk is that the hardened gate is a false negative at m=256, and that the fp32 candidate loses there on extra bytes.
justification: A. The mechanism is measured, not conjectured. In ce808e5a, candidate N (the NN halves, view of pooler_t) ran nvjet 128x128 NNT 24.7 us + add 2.1 us at m=256, against master's nvjet 128x64 NNT 28.8. At m=128 it ran nvjet 128x64 NNT 20.1 + add 1.5, against master's splitK NNT 20.8 + splitKreduce 3.0 (FINDINGS: master 741072dc rows 22.85 / 27.98). The floors are 14.6 / 17.4 us, so both rows are still 1.3-1.6x off their floors and the direction holds. The expected shapes match TASK.md: only the two verify pooler rows move, and decode m<=32 is routed earlier in kernel_fn and stays untouched. No test runs pooler at m=128/256, and m=512/1000 stay on master. The prior field is accurate. pooler-k-halves-batched-gemm-m65-m256 is the same mechanism, and FINDINGS' auto-generated 'Do not try' lists it as neutral/within-ci. But its rows won and it was never landed (DIAGNOSIS #7, Action 1), so this is a restack, not a retry; the differences (new base, fp32 candidate, harder gate) are real. The run is still expected to come out neutral on the headline: +0.5-0.9% against a margin of at least 1.5%. Its value is per-row confirmation on the current base and acting as the depends_on parent for combo-verify-cells-pooler-khalf-plus-qkv-rowowner-m8-m16. WEAKEST LINK: the new gate against the measured margins. In ce808e5a's own prepare log the single-round master/cand was 1.069 at m=128 but only 1.037 at m=256 (IQR 0.90 vs 1.34), while the judge gave about 1.12 at m=256. The prepare gate under-predicts this cell. Two independent rounds that must both be >= 1.03 will plausibly drop m=256 to master by chance, which would be a gate false negative, not a refutation. Second-weakest: candidate (b) at m=256 is not free. Its fp32 partials double the GEMM epilogue write (8 MB vs 4 MB) and the add's read (8 MB fp32 vs 4 MB bf16). A mixed-dtype torch.add(out=bf16) also leaves PyTorch's vectorized_elementwise path for the slower dynamic-cast/unrolled one. I estimate about +1.5-2.5 us over (a), which would put (b) near parity with master at m=256 (about 27-29 vs 28.8). The fp32 C type may also change cuBLAS's tile heuristic for the bmm, away from the 128x128 that made (a) win. (b) is likelier to pay at m=128, where the incumbent already runs a fp32 splitKreduce.
confounders: pooler-nn-layout-widen-m256 (landed): it owns nn_p256_ok and the incumbent at m=256 (NN torch.mm on pooler_t), and candidate N reuses pooler_t. The gate's 'flag off' arm must run master's NN path, so nn_p256_ok must already be True when the khalf gate runs inside _prepare_state. Otherwise the baseline silently becomes dispatch TNT (about 30-31 us) and the gate is inflated.

restack-three-cell-wins-router-unpooler-cluster-m8-nn-m128 (landed): it owns nn_ok, which is shared with unpooler m=128. Master's _ab_component(layer, m) has no state argument and maps pooler m=128 to nn_ok, and pooler 128/256 are already AB_CASES entries. Unless _ab_component returns pooler_khalf_ok first for the cells that were routed (the prior patch added a state parameter to do this), a self-check miss on the khalf path turns off nn_ok as well, and the resulting unpooler verify_16 regression would be misread as this hypothesis's effect. Do not add duplicate AB_CASES entries; remap the component instead.

combo-rowowner-reduce-free-m1-qkv-o-plus-naive (landed, the current base): it adds the cuBLASLt qkv m=128 cell (own workspace and plan) and bulk m=1 cells, so qkv_gate shares the verify_16 load with the pooler but not its graph. The judge times each shape in its own graph with a cold L2, so I expect no direct interaction. The one effect is that its _cell_gate/_ab_flags machinery is what the new flag must plug into (NEW_CELL_FLAGS and second-state inheritance).

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (landed): it remains the fallback when nn_ok or nn_p256_ok is off. If FINAL FLAGS shows either NN flag False, the comparison baseline has shifted and attribution against 741072dc is void.
interference: No companion. (i) An ab-revert of either NN-layout hypothesis would recreate a stale incumbent, and candidate N needs pooler_t anyway. (ii) There is nothing to tune: two halves is the conjecture, and the bf16-vs-fp32 question is answered in-process by the selector, which times master, (a) and (b) on the same synthetic x in the same run. (iii) The bf16-partials control already exists as ce808e5a, the same mechanism judged on the previous base, with kernel names recorded. A gain or a loss is therefore readable from one run if the build prints the following for both m: both rounds' medians and IQRs for master, (a) and (b); the kernel names for (a) and (b), even when not routed; which candidate was routed; and FINAL FLAGS (nn_ok, nn_p256_ok, pooler_khalf_ok). Judge rows by the per-shape paired speedup against SGLang, not by absolute microseconds. Master's own pooler m=256 row varied 27.98-30.05 us across today's runs (about 7%), so a us-delta against one prior run is not reliable. If the gate keeps master at m=256, log it as 'gate false negative / not measured', not as a refutation, since the judge already measured about 1.12x there.
rules_flags: None blocking. Weights stay bf16 (a view of master's lossless NN repack); fp32 appears only in internal partials; bf16 partials passed every test (rel L2 2.45e-3, bound 1e-2), and single-nonzero rows stay exact because the other half's dot product is exactly 0.

kernel_fn must gate on cfg m and state flags only, with no print, try or sync. A torch.empty for the output inside kernel_fn is fine under graph capture. Do not keep a persistent fp32 partials buffer in state that is reused across calls unless it is fully overwritten each call (it is), and never derive it from data.
The selector must use synthetic x in prepare() only and choose once, on state A; B inherits through _ab_flags so the A and B graphs run the same path.
open_questions: Does torch.bmm(xh, wh, out_dtype=torch.float32) exist and accept the strided xh (strides 4096, 8192, 1) on torch 2.14.1 without inserting a contiguous() copy? Print xh.stride() and assert no copy kernel in the profile, as the prior run did.

Will the profiler name assertion accept candidate (b)'s add kernel? A mixed-dtype add may launch unrolled_elementwise_kernel rather than vectorized_elementwise_kernel, and a name filter copied from the prior patch could falsely reject (b).
Does a fp32 C type change cuBLAS's bmm tile choice at m=256 away from 128x128 (the source of the win)? Print (b)'s GEMM kernel name.

Master's _cell_gate returns medians only. The hardened IQR <= 1.5x criterion needs an extended gate that also returns IQRs; the prior run's N at m=128 had IQR 0.96 against master 0.70 (1.37x), close to the limit.

The single-round m=256 margin was 1.037 while the judge measured about 1.12. Should m=256 keep the 1.03 two-round bar (risk: a false negative that makes the run a no-op on that row), or should the gate record both rounds so the orchestrator can decide? At minimum, the outcome must distinguish 'gate rejected' from 'row lost'.
The queued combo depends_on this branch. If the gate routes only m=128 here, does the combo re-gate m=256 itself, or inherit the master route?
